set.body:
MEASURED ON REAL DATA, well-sampled: more than half of every rdm_sampling_covariance() call is spent re-deriving fit-invariant capability information, not computing the covariance.

Profile of 60 consecutive calls on the Haxby VT exemplar configuration - 577 features, 577 centres, mean support 44.8, q = 8, fixed-identity metric - with the JIT warmed by 5 prior calls. 3192 samples at 2 ms:

  TOTAL TIME
    .require_relation_fit_capability      53.4 percent
    relation_fit_capabilities             53.0 percent
    .validate_relation                    17.8 percent
    grepl                                 14.2 percent
    .additive_frame_signature              9.5 percent
    .validate_frame_for_compile            6.8 percent
    .validate_effect_space_shallow         5.9 percent
    .validate_effect_extractor_shallow     5.6 percent

  SELF TIME, top entries
    grepl                14.2 percent
    serialize             5.9 percent
    deparse               4.4 percent
    make.names            3.5 percent
    digest::digest        2.6 percent

  per-call mean, steady state: 0.106 s

TWO THINGS THE PROFILE SAYS PLAINLY.

First, relation_fit_capabilities() is recomputed on every call and costs more than half of it. That result is a property of the FIT, which does not change across nodes of a sweep. Computing it once and carrying it - on the fit, or on the plan - would remove roughly half the per-call cost at a stroke, with no change to any number the function returns.

Second, the presence of serialize, deparse, make.names and digest::digest in the top self-time entries, together with .additive_frame_signature at 9.5 percent, says signatures are being recomputed per call. Signatures are content identity; for a fixed plan and a fixed fit they cannot change between node 1 and node 577.

THIS VINDICATES THE ORIGINAL INSTINCT ON bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC even though its headline figures did not reproduce. That bead suspected "per-call recomputation of plan/fit-invariant work (residual factorization, contrasts, validation)". Validation was the right guess. It is now quantified: 53 percent, and it is capability derivation specifically rather than residual work.

SCALE OF THE PRIZE, stated conservatively. At a steady-state 0.106 s/node a 577-centre sweep is about 61 seconds. Removing the capability re-derivation would take that toward 30 seconds. That is not the difference between usable and unusable - the arm is already usable, contrary to what the README currently says - but it is a straightforward halving of the cost of the package's most expensive documented operation, and the work removed is provably invariant.

CAVEAT. Profiler attribution can mislead when functions are inlined or when a cheap function is called very many times. The 53 percent figure should be confirmed by the implementer before anyone restructures around it - ideally by caching the capability result behind a flag and re-measuring, which is a smaller change than the precompute-once object the parent bead proposes and would test the hypothesis directly.

Filed separately from the parent bead because that one is about a cost claim I could not reproduce, whereas this is a cost I did measure, on the current tree, with enough samples to trust.
set.title: Over half of every rdm_sampling_covariance() call is fit-invariant capability re-derivation
